question: A bookkeeping firm is planning its first Azure virtual machines and asks which factors will directly influence the monthly compute charge. Which **three** of the following affect the cost of running an Azure virtual machine? (Select three.)

options.text: The size and series of the virtual machine (vCPUs, memory, hardware generation)
The region in which the virtual machine is deployed
How long the virtual machine runs — compute is billed only while it is allocated
The number of resource groups in the subscription
The number of tags applied to the virtual machine

explanation:
Three factors on this list directly drive VM compute cost:

- **Size and series** — Bigger VMs with more vCPUs and memory cost more per hour, and different series (general purpose, compute optimized, GPU) carry different rates for the hardware they provide.
- **Region** — The same VM size is priced differently in different regions, reflecting local infrastructure, energy, and market costs.
- **Runtime / consumption** — Compute is a metered, consumption-based charge: you pay while the VM is allocated, and a **stopped (deallocated)** VM stops accruing compute charges (attached disks continue to bill as storage).

**Why not the other options:**
- **The number of resource groups** — Resource groups are free logical containers; how resources are organized has no effect on their price.
- **The number of tags** — Tags are free metadata used for organization and cost *reporting*; applying them never changes what a resource costs.
